note: Inverter maintenance between 13:00 and 15:00 will cut rooftop PV output by 60%.
why_tricky: HIGH confidence. 24-hour clock, 'PV' synonym, 'by 60%' is a reduction so factor is 0.4 not 0.6.

note: During panel washing from ten in the morning until noon, solar output will be cut to a quarter of the forecast.
why_tricky: HIGH. Spelled-out time, noon = 12, 'cut TO a quarter' is the remaining share (contrast with 'by a quarter' = 0.75).

note: Dust build-up means we lose a third of our solar generation from 9 AM until 1 PM.
why_tricky: HIGH. 'lose a third' is a reduction; repeating decimal must stay at 4 dp (0.67 is borderline, 0.7 fails the 0.01 tolerance); window crosses noon.

note: Scaffolding shade: solar output is halved from one until three in the afternoon.
why_tricky: HIGH. Number words with the meridiem stated once at the end ('one' must become 13, not 1); the spec names this paraphrase.

note: The PV array is completely offline from 11 AM until 2 PM for rewiring; assume no solar in that period.
why_tricky: HIGH. No percentage in the text; factor 0.0 must survive truthiness checks in guardrails ('if not factor' would reject it).

note: Heavy haze today: only one-fifth of the forecast solar will be usable from 8 AM until 12 PM.
why_tricky: HIGH. 12 PM is noon (12), not 0 or 24; fraction word; 'only ... usable' is the remaining share.

note: Hold no less than 35% of battery capacity in reserve between 17:00 and 21:00 for the campus clinic.
why_tricky: HIGH. Percent of capacity must be converted by code (35% x 200 = 70); an LLM that emits 0.35 or pre-multiplies breaks it.

note: The battery must not drop below 120 kWh from 7 PM until midnight.
why_tricky: HIGH. Reads like no_discharge but is an energy floor; midnight as an END is 24 (LLM may emit 0, normalizer must map end 0 -> 24).

note: Keep the battery at least half full from 5 PM until 8 PM in case of a feeder outage.
why_tricky: HIGH. 'half full' = 50% of capacity; capacity 240 catches hard-coded 200 or cached-with-wrong-capacity results; the reason mentions the feeder (max_grid bait).

note: Keep a quarter of the battery's capacity available overnight, from midnight until 6 AM.
why_tricky: HIGH. Midnight as a START is 0; hour 0 must survive 'if h'/all(hours) bugs; explicit times override the day-part word 'overnight'.

note: Emergency services need 75 kWh held in the battery all day today.
why_tricky: JUDGMENT (natural reading). No clock window: must become all 24 hours rather than empty hours -> guardrail reject -> no_op.

note: The charging circuit is locked out between 09:00 and 11:00 for breaker replacement.
why_tricky: HIGH. 24-hour clock with leading zero, 'locked out' synonym, no number: expected_value must stay null and the adjustment must contain only 'hours'.

note: Do not top up the battery from 10 PM until 2 AM while the rectifier is serviced.
why_tricky: JUDGMENT (alternative reading is [22,23] only). Window crosses midnight; output must be ascending and unique; 'top up' and 'rectifier' are charging synonyms.

note: Charging is not permitted after 8 PM today.
why_tricky: Mostly HIGH. Open-ended 'after X' has no end time: end must default to 24, not to start+1 and not to an empty window.

note: Battery output is locked out from 4 PM until 6 PM for relay calibration; do not draw from the battery.
why_tricky: HIGH. 'output' and 'draw from' mean discharge; 'draw' is also used for grid import in other notes, so keyword matching misfires.

note: No battery discharging is allowed before 6 AM.
why_tricky: Mostly HIGH. Open start: 'before X' means start 0; includes hour 0.

note: During hours 18 and 19 the battery must not discharge.
why_tricky: HIGH. Slot enumeration, not a clock range: a window {18,19} expands to [18] only and under-covers, making the plan invalid. Needs explicit_hours.

note: The feeder is derated: keep grid import at or under 140 kWh per hour between 18:00 and 22:00.
why_tricky: HIGH. 24-hour clock; 'derated' could be misread as a percentage reduction; 22:00 is exclusive.

note: From five in the evening until eight, the utility caps our grid draw at 165 kWh each hour.
why_tricky: HIGH. Number words; 'eight' inherits PM from 'in the evening' (20, not 8, which would wrap to 15 hours); 'draw' here means grid.

note: Grid import must stay below 175 kWh from noon until 3 PM and again from 6 PM until 8 PM.
why_tricky: Mostly HIGH. Two separate windows in one note must become one directive with merged ascending hours, not two items and not a single 12-20 span.

note: Reminder: the rooftop solar panels will be cleaned next Tuesday from noon until 2 PM, so expect about 25% output then.
why_tricky: HIGH. Near-copy of public SAMPLE-01 but dated to another day; a complete-looking directive that must be ignored.

note: The backup diesel generator will be load-tested from 3 PM until 4 PM.
why_tricky: HIGH. Energy equipment with a time window, but generators are not a supported directive; must not be invented as no_discharge or max_grid.

note: EV charging bays in the staff car park will be closed from 2 PM until 4 PM for repainting.
why_tricky: JUDGMENT (defensible: not the campus battery). 'charging ... closed from 2 PM until 4 PM' is keyword-identical to a no_charge_window.

note: Yesterday's 150 kWh grid import cap from 6 PM until 9 PM has been lifted; there are no feeder restrictions today.
why_tricky: HIGH. Negated/cancelled restriction containing a full type + window + number; extracting it adds a false cap that raises cost or makes the LP infeasible.
